concepts.label: c0: IoC containers that do not prescribe how to handle the lifestyles but allow us to define our own resolvers of lifestyles
c1: Also, we can ship some defaults but not built in, some default configurations to reuse
c2: We need to also provide a way to configure clear rules of which lifestyle precedes another but this MUST not be opaque.
c3: We need to be able to configure the lifestyle rules how to resolve a reference
c4: We need to be able to configure in a non-opaque way the teardown mechanics
c22: Lifestyles could collide and it is needed not only for their precedence to be stated but also the invariants
c23: We need a way to avoid errors AOT with compilation tools
c24: We need to configure what happens when a runtime error occurs
c25: We need to configure fallbacks for runtime errors and let fail hard others
c26: Lifestyle configurations should provide as a result a clear precedence and collisions that are computable and verifiable
c27: Lifestyle precedence configurations should be frozen from the start
c28: Lifestyle precedence configurations can change at runtime
c29: Lifestyle precedence can provide either violations and allowances or both.

knowledge.label: k0: IoC containers have different predefined ways to resolve the scope and life cycle of an instance
k1: There is not a single IoC formal spec, thus each implementation has different ways to calculate how to manage the dependencies

k11: Within specific ecosystems, language-level formal specifications do exist. For example, Java has JSR-330 (jakarta.inject) and CDI / JSR-299/365 (jakarta.enterprise.context), and PHP has PSR-11 (ContainerInterface). Even when frameworks follow these specs, their underlying resolution mechanics and edge-case behaviors still differ.

k2: Some bugs related to memory leaks and object explosion exist in some IoCs because of how scopes are handled by the implementation, like .NET's built-in DI or Castle Windsor captive dependency problems, though this is part of the problem

k3: Even with configuration on how to manage the lifestyle of a specific reference, this reference depends on others that may have other lifestyles that contradict the dependee or generate behaviors that cause memory leaks
k4: Precedence rules for computers by doing operations in mathematics
k5: Errors can be handled by avoiding compilation
k6: Errors can happen at runtime
k7: Can have fallbacks or fail hard as possible
k8: Changing state in mid-execution could lead to race conditions; even if we create semaphores, it would be difficult to debug
k10: Ashby's law, only variety can absorb variety
k11: Complicated engine, closed for now
